name: Open Channel: Meridian Dispatch
description: The oldest continuously operating pirate broadcast in GLMZ, running since the city's formal corponation consolidation in 2183, Open Channel began as a community radio format and has evolved through four distinct technological generations — analog, early mesh, encrypted neural-adjacent broadcast, and its current distributed node architecture — while maintaining its founding commitment to unfiltered Shelf community reporting. Unlike the Null Brief's document-focused journalism, Open Channel is explicitly testimonial: real people, voice-modulated or face-obscured, describing what is happening to them in real time. It has been shut down officially at least nine times. It has never actually stopped.
cultural_impact: Open Channel's forty-year continuity makes it the institutional memory of the Shelf in a way that no licensed media outlet can replicate, and its archive — distributed across thousands of physical nodes — is considered the most comprehensive record of corponation activity in Tier 1 in existence.
story_hooks: Someone has been systematically destroying Open Channel's physical archive nodes — not to silence current broadcasts, but to erase specific historical testimony from the early 2190s.

A Tier 5 archivist contacts the broadcast claiming to have an authenticated copy of Open Channel's complete archive, and wants to donate it to a licensed institution — but the collective doesn't trust their motives.

A current Open Channel correspondent has been approached by Vantablack Media with an offer to license the show's format, and the collective is fracturing over whether legitimacy is the same thing as survival.
